title: Woollarawarre Bennelong
summary: A Wangal man born around 1764 on the south shore of the Parramatta River, Bennelong was seized at Manly Cove on 25 November 1789 on the orders of Governor Phillip. He became a go-between and interpreter, and a house was built for him on what is now Bennelong Point. He sailed to England in December 1792, was back by September 1795, and died at Kissing Point on 3 January 1813.

uncertainty.note: The Australian Museum gives birth around 1764; the Dictionary of Sydney gives his age as about 24 in January 1788. Both give death on 3 January 1813 at Kissing Point and his capture at Manly Cove.

where.modern_name: Bennelong Point, Sydney, New South Wales, Australia (pinned to the point where Governor Phillip had a house built for him; he was taken at Manly Cove and died at Kissing Point, Putney)
where.historical_name: Bennelong Point at Sydney Cove, colony of New South Wales (the house stood where the point now bears his name)

importance.justification: The Australian Museum describes him as the first Aboriginal man to visit Europe and return, and a go-between for Governor Phillip.

audience_note: This record covers the abduction of an Aboriginal man by British colonial authorities and the effects of colonisation, including a smallpox epidemic in which the Dictionary of Sydney says his first wife died. It names a person who has died.

reviewer_note: Birth is approximate (c. 1764; about 24 in January 1788). His clan and the three places he is tied to (Manly Cove, Bennelong Point, Kissing Point) differ; the pin is Bennelong Point because it is the only one linked to his documented role as intermediary. Return date is given as September 1795 by the Australian Museum only.
